title: Optical Clearing and Imaging of Fluorescently Labeled Ex Vivo Rat Brain Slices
author: Giacomoni, Habekost, et al.
materials: Donkey anti-rabbit IgG (H + L), Alexa Fluor 647

steps.title: Sterilize tools and don PPE
steps.instruction: Autoclave all surgical instruments and materials; wear protective gloves, safety goggles, protective clothing, and a face mask.

steps.title: Clean cutting station and vibratome
steps.instruction: Wash benchtop, vibratome, buffer tray, and tubing with water then 70 % ethanol; submerge razor blade in 70 % ethanol and let dry for 5 min.

steps.title: Set up vibratome and cooling
steps.instruction: Insert razor blade into holder, turn vibratome on, check blade position with VibroCheck, install double‑walled buffer tray, connect silicone tube to a gas diffuser (micro‑filter‑candle or aquarium air curtain), turn on cooling unit and set temperature to 3 °C at least 10 min before use.

steps.title: Prepare chilled aCSF buffer
steps.instruction: Fill buffer tray with 300 mL pre‑chilled NMDG‑HEPES aCSF and maintain low carbogen bubbling to keep turbulence minimal.

steps.title: Arrange dissection tools
steps.instruction: Place vibratome specimen plate, straight forceps, Moria perforated spoon, glass petri dish, single Whatman round filter paper, liquid super glue, and one razor blade on the benchtop next to the vibratome.

steps.title: Prepare dissection solutions
steps.instruction: Add 80 mL pre‑chilled NMDG‑HEPES aCSF to a 100 mL beaker, keep on ice and bubble with carbogen using a small micro‑filter‑candle; prepare 50 mL wash buffer and keep under continuous carbogen bubbling with a micro‑filter‑candle.

steps.title: Dissect brain and collect tissue
steps.instruction: Decapitate animal with rodent guillotine after depth anesthesia (pentobarbital sodium 30–50 mg/kg i.p.). Remove scalp skin, make a 1 cm lateral/ventral incision through basioccipital bone into foramen magnum, cut dorsally along interparietal, parietal and frontal bones to nasal bone, transect nasal bone at premaxilla, remove nasal, frontal, parietal and interparietal bones rostral‑to‑caudal with straight bone cutter, rinse brain with 10 mL pre‑chilled NMDG‑HEPES aCSF saturated with carbogen, and gently scoop out the intact brain into the beaker.

steps.title: Mount brain block on vibratome
steps.instruction: Place brain on Whatman round filter paper in a 100 × 15 mm glass petri dish, remove olfactory bulb and cerebellum for cortical coronal slices and glue the brain vertically; lift tissue block with straight forceps, fix to specimen plate with enough liquid super glue, and immediately transfer plate into the chilled NMDG‑HEPES aCSF buffer tray.

steps.title: Section brain into slices
steps.instruction: Set vibratome speed to 0.14 mm/s, amplitude to 1.10 mm, and slice thickness to 275 µm; start sectioning from ventral to dorsal. Complete tissue block preparation within 30 s to preserve slice quality.

steps.title: Fix slices with PFA
steps.instruction: Remove culture medium, add 1 mL 4 % paraformaldehyde (pH 7.4) to the well and an additional 1 mL on top of each brain slice; fix for 20 min at room temperature (20–23 °C). Transfer each fixed slice to a glass vial with 1 mL KPBS using a paintbrush, then wash 2 × 5 min with 1 mL KPBS per vial at room temperature.

steps.title: Store fixed slices (pause)
steps.instruction: Place fixed and washed slices at 4 °C in bacteriostatic preservative (0.01 % sodium azide in KPBS); slices remain stable for a few weeks.

steps.title: Permeabilize and block slices
steps.instruction: Remove KPBS, add 1 mL blocking solution to each vial, and incubate overnight at room temperature (20–23 °C) or for two days at 4 °C.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Prepare primary antibody solution (rabbit anti‑Iba1 diluted 1:1000 in 1 mL blocking solution), remove blocking solution, add 1 mL primary antibody solution, and incubate for 48–72 h at room temperature (20–23 °C).

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Remove primary antibody solution and wash the slice 3 × 20 min with KPBS at room temperature on a shaking platform at 100 RPM.

steps.title: Prepare secondary antibody mix
steps.instruction: Dilute secondary antibody 1:200 in 1 mL blocking solution and add DAPI 1:1000; keep the solution protected from light (e.g., cover with aluminum foil).

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Remove KPBS, add 1 mL secondary antibody solution, and incubate for 24–48 h at room temperature (20–23 °C).

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Remove secondary antibody solution and wash 3 × 20 min with KPBS at room temperature on a shaking platform at 100 RPM.

steps.title: Store stained slices (pause)
steps.instruction: Place immunostained slices at 4 °C in 0.01 % sodium azide in KPBS, protected from light; stable for up to two weeks, though imaging is recommended sooner to avoid fluorescence loss.

description: Brain slices, either as acute preparations or as organotypic cultures, represent physiologically relevant three-dimensional ex vivo platform widely used for the investigation of neuronal circuitry and cellular/molecular mechanism of the brain. For decades, they have been invaluable for electrophysiological studies,1,2,3 modeling of neurodegenerative diseases,4,5 and evaluation of therapeutic options prior to in vivo investigations.6 However, microscopy strategies coupled with optical tissue clearing remain largely unexplored for brain slices even though deep tissue imaging with cellular resolution poses a major challenge in non-cleared tissue.7 Here, we describe a detailed protocol for cutting, immunofluorescent labeling, and clearing to facilitate imaging of acute/cultured brain slices. The methodology provides a low-cost and simple solution for optical access throughout the entire thickness of the brain slice (250–300 μm) to reveal structural information otherwise lost in non-cleared tissue. Refractive index matching is based on ethyl cinnamate, a non-toxic compound that can be handled and used on microscope systems without special safety measures.8,9 Furthermore, the tissue flattening demonstrated here reduces time for image acquisition and leads to smaller file sizes. As such, this simple and reliable protocol is intended to be routinely used for imaging and histological analysis of ex vivo brain slices. Notably, the culture system presented here is suitable for ex vivo pre-clinical validation of therapeutics, viral transduction screening, and genetic manipulations (i.e., transgene delivery10). We have tested this protocol using ex vivo preparations from female Sprague-Dawley and athymic nude rats of four to fifteen months of age.
